narrative:
The model estimates a 66% chance that you will leave your current job, which is why your promotion request has been denied. This prediction is driven primarily by three key factors in your profile.

Your relatively short overall work experience of 1-5 years was the strongest factor pushing the model toward predicting you will stay. Most employees the model expects to remain with their organizations also fall into this early-career group, so the system sees your limited total experience as a stabilizing element rather than a risk.

However, two other aspects pulled more strongly in the opposite direction. The fact that you have received other job offers while working here was the second most influential factor and worked to increase the likelihood of leaving. Having external opportunities often signals that an employee is actively considering or being recruited elsewhere. Additionally, your feeling that your job lacks long-term security and stability was the third important driver and further increased the predicted chance of departure. Many employees the model expects to stay report a clearer sense of job security.

Taken together, the combination of outside opportunities and perceived instability outweighed the stabilizing effect of your early-career stage, leading to the 66% probability of leaving.

The organization should discuss your sense of job stability and explore whether clearer career paths or retention measures could address your concerns. You may also wish to reflect on how external offers align with your longer-term goals.
